- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2), model underreacts; adjust downward bias by +0.5–1.5% to align with true mean reversion.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast peak.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if 30-day forecast is >85% of recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overfitting.
- If sentiment history includes 0.4 or higher, model should not assume continuation of trend; introduce 1–2% downward bias to reflect market cooling.
